title: AAP Issues Guidance on Generative AI Use by Clinicians
source_used: American Academy of Pediatrics press release, carried by Mirage News
key_facts: The American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) published a policy statement on the safe, equitable and effective use of generative AI in pediatric clinical care.

The statement, 'Recommendations for the Development and Implementation of Generative Artificial Intelligence Tools in Pediatric Clinical Care', appears in the November 2026 issue of Pediatrics and was published online on 3 Oct 2026.
It was presented on 3 Oct 2026 at the AAP National Conference and Exhibition in San Diego; co-author R. Brandon Hunter presents a session on 4 Oct 2026.

AAP says most generative AI tools are trained on data where children are underrepresented and few are rigorously evaluated in pediatrics; tools should be designed for children, not adapted from adult models.
The statement calls for patient privacy and security safeguards, bias reduction, pediatric datasets, diverse representation and rigorous human oversight and accountability.
It covers only clinicians' use of generative AI in pediatric care, not direct use by children and families; separate family guidance is in preparation.
Lead author is Srinivasan Suresh; the statement was developed by the AAP Council on Clinical Information Technology and the Section on Innovation in Therapeutics and Technology.
quote_evidence: Patient privacy and security must be at the forefront of AI, and tools need to be specifically designed for pediatric care, rather than adapted from adult models, according to the statement
"There will be a need for rigorous human oversight and accountability." (Srinivasan Suresh)
"adoption is often moving faster than the evidence on how to use these tools effectively is being produced." (R. Brandon Hunter)
why_it_matters_hint: The main US pediatricians' body sets the first formal expectations for generative AI tools used on children, which developers and hospitals will be measured against.
notes: Mirage News is a press-release carrier; the text is the AAP's own release, so the source is the AAP. No aap.org link was in the text; url is the page where the release was read.
